rv.q: McElroen's "Debate: Baldwin vs. Buckley" is on a long U.S./U.K. tour with these two actors.
This is a theatre production that entertains as well as educates and challenges audiences.

Even more so during Black History Month 2025. Among Baldwin’s many, many gifts was prescience. As a gay Black midcentury man, he wrote about the many discriminations in his own time that are, sadly, also applicable in our current moment.
The immersive locale almost becomes another character in this 90-minute production.
Under McElroen’s masterful direction, Teagle F. Bougere (Baldwin) and Eric T. Miller (Buckley) are superb.
Precisely 60 years after the real debate, watching it now brought to life by these brilliant actors will galvanize your brain.
Miller's skin-crawling unctuousness and flashes of condescension stand in contrast to Bougere's contained but razor-sharp dissection of the ugly truths of race in America.
"Debate” is pre-scripted docudrama—an outward sketch of history, rather than an inward exploration of its implications and effects.
Baldwin here is poetic and theatrical, and Bougere's rendering of him is quite excellent.

Whether the actors agreed or disagreed with the words they spoke, all of them did a great job in bringing this historic event to life and pointing up the enduring history of racial division in the United States.
